name: Sranan Tongo
notes: Sranan Tongo (Sranantongo), the English-lexifier creole lingua franca of Suriname, with heavy Dutch and West African (Gbe, Kikongo) input. The mapping follows the official 1986 phonology-based spelling fixed by Resolution 4501 of 15 July 1986: ⟨ò⟩ = /ɔ/, ⟨sy⟩ = /ʃ/, ⟨ty dy⟩ = /t͡ʃ d͡ʒ/, ⟨aw ow⟩ = the diphthongs /au̯ ou̯/. English is the lexifier, not an ancestor node in this graph. This spec transcribes that standard and nothing else, which is a deliberate boundary rather than a gap, so it is worth stating what falls outside it. Suriname wrote Sranan in a Dutch-based spelling before 1986, and the 1986 rules are stated as prohibitions against it: never ⟨ie⟩ but ⟨i⟩, never ⟨oe⟩ but ⟨u⟩, never ⟨j⟩ but ⟨y⟩ (so ⟨tjari djari⟩ become ⟨tyari dyari⟩), never doubled ⟨aa ee oo⟩ or doubled consonants, never ⟨z⟩ or ⟨v⟩. Pre-1986 forms are therefore not loanwords carrying Dutch phonology; they are the SAME Sranan words in a superseded spelling, and the WikiPron gold this spec is scored against carries both spellings of six of them side by side (boegroe/bugru, loekoe/luku, markoesa/markusa, sibiboesi/sibibusi, kapoewa/kapuwa, kapoeweri/kapuweri). Of the gold's 702 distinct words, 29 break at least one 1986 rule and the engine fails 27 of them, which is 27 of its 118 total exact-match misses. Two boundaries must not be confused. The sequences the standard forbids outright — ⟨ie oe aa ee oo⟩ and anything containing ⟨j⟩ — cannot occur in conformant text at all, so giving them legacy values would collide with nothing. The sequences ⟨ui⟩ and ⟨uw⟩ are ordinary conformant spellings of vowel-plus-glide (muiti, kapuwa, antruwa, puiri) and giving them their Dutch values breaks nine words in this gold that are correct today. A separate pre-1986 variant spec is the place for the legacy readings if they are ever wanted; folding them into this table would make one spec claim two orthographies. Out-of-orthography input is currently handled by dropping the unmapped letters, so ⟨Venezuela⟩ comes out as `enezuela` and ⟨gevaarlijk⟩ as `ɡeaaɾlik`; that silent deletion is a general engine behaviour, not specific to Sranan.

orthography_standard.name: Officiële spelling voor het Sranan(-tongo), Resolutie van 15 juli 1986 No. 4501
orthography_standard.authority: Government of Suriname, on the report of the Spellingcommissie Sranan
orthography_standard.notes: The phonology-based spelling this spec's grapheme table implements. The linked short manual reproduces the resolution's twelve rules; it is published by Stichting Volkslectuur Suriname in Woordenlijst Sranan-Nederlands/Nederlands-Sranan/English-Sranan (Paramaribo: Vaco, 1995), pp. 34-35.

sources.author: Stichting Volkslectuur Suriname
sources.title: Korte handleiding voor de spelling van het Sranan volgens de Resolutie van 15 juli 1986 No. 4501, in Woordenlijst Sranan-Nederlands/Nederlands-Sranan/English-Sranan
sources.notes: Retrieved and read in full. The twelve rules of the official 1986 spelling, each stated as a prohibition with wrong/right example pairs: never ie but i (pasie/pasi, lobie/lobi), never word-final ng but n (tang/tan), never doubled consonants (passi/pasi, nakki/naki), never aa (waarti/warti), never ee but ei (dee/dei, pree/prei), never oe but u (boekoe/buku, foeroe/furu), never oo but ow (skootu/skowtu), never j but y (jari/yari, taja/taya, djari/dyari, tjari/tyari), never y as the second half of a diphthong (bay/bai, dey/dei), never z or v but s and f (zabi/sabi, vri/fri). Those example pairs are the evidence that pre-1986 spellings are the same Sranan lexemes rather than Dutch loanwords, and they are what fixes the boundary of the grapheme table in this spec.

ancestors.notes: English lexifier (with later Portuguese and Dutch relexification/borrowing layers); Sranan Tongo of Suriname. Holm (1989:434-445); APiCS ch. 1 (Winford & Plag).
Gbe (Ewe/Fon) substrate: tone/pitch-accent tendencies, TMA system, serial verbs.
Portuguese relexification/adstrate layer from early plantation contact (shared with the maroon creoles).
